items.title: Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different

(Image credit: HoYoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nodusfall has been Gamescom's biggest surprise: a new co-op action romp from the masters of gacha, HoYoverse, which seemingly does away with so much of what we all associate with the developer.

HoYoverse's games are normally vibrant anime affairs full of waifus and himbos waiting to be collected by thirsty players. Even as the genres and systems change from game to game, the studio has a distinct style and design philosophy—one that's been incredibly successful.

Instead of resting on its laurels, however, HoYoverse is taking a big swing with Nodusfall. One of the most fundamental changes is that characters are not obtained through random draws . This is not your typical gacha game. Indeed, HoYoverse hasn't confirmed any gacha mechanics yet—though we do know that cosmetic monetisation is being considered.

When it was first unveiled during Gamescom's Opening Night Live, the immediate comparisons being bandied around were Elden Ring and Monster Hunter, both of which are fair comparisons but which don't really tell the whole story. That they are inspirations seems undeniable, but Nodusfall is absolutely doing its own thing here.

First of all: Nodusfall is not remotely a soulslike. What it has in common with Elden Ring, then, is largely aesthetic and vibes. As HoYoverse describes it, the world of Nodusfall is one where "divine authority has crumbled and order has collapsed". It's simultaneously bleak and beautiful.

HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter Mistfall Hunter's demo might finally convince me, a souls sicko, to give extraction games a proper go—even if it's more modern God of War than Nightreign Nodusfall First Reveal Trailer: "Wield Divinity, Sever the Dreadnodus" - YouTube Watch On Monster Hunter is a closer relative. Solo adventurers and groups can select contracts, and then go out into the world to hunt down big beasties. These are lengthy, elaborate fights with multiple phases, taking place in spacious outdoor areas. So yeah, this all felt immediately evocative of Monster Hunter. But the similarities largely end there.

My four-player crew started off in a hub area, where we could select and customise our characters—one of which had two classes, while the rest had one. I opted for a serious looking lad with a big sword, serving as the group's tank. So you're not just creating a customisable blank slate who is defined by whatever weapon they happen to be holding.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Each character has dramatically different combat styles and unique mechanics, so while I was going to spend the next 30 minutes blocking damage with my huge weapon and sticking to foes like angry velcro, another member of the party was going to spend that same time hanging back and healing my reckless ass. Nodusfall isn't an RPG, but it does have an RPG's role-based classes.

Our HoYoverse babysitter led us to our battles—three boss-style scraps with an escalating level of challenge, culminating in a massive brawl against a huge dragon and its giant, heavily-armoured rider. There wasn't much time for faffing in the open area, though I did clock other creatures ambling around—but we were here for larger prey.

It's more aggressive and spammy than Monster Hunter, but some precision is still required.

Even as a slow tank, I was surprisingly agile. Unless you've volunteered for healer duty, Nodusfall is a brisk, relentless kind of action game, where you'll be stringing together impressively flashy combos as you keep an eye on your skill cooldowns. And all the while, you'll feel like a human shaped missile, always launching yourself at whatever creature is in your sights.

The next game in a huge Chinese action RPG series has plenty of action, but I hope it hasn't totally abandoned the RPG An absurdly large patch filled with over 2K lines of changes is how the devs of early access co-op RPG Fellowship hope to hook players on running MMO-like dungeons without the MMO 18 embargoes from Summer Game Fest just lifted, so let's rank everything I saw in LA It's more aggressive and spammy than Monster Hunter, but some precision is still required. I became rather fond of the clash mechanic, where you charge up a strong attack, and release it right as the monster is about to hit you, countering the attack. It helps that I looked stylish doing it, with my already massive sword growing, transforming into a magical, glowing WMD.

items.title: ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition and new content for ELDEN RING beckon back players to the lands between
items.summary: ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition launches on Nintendo Switch 2, with new classes, armor sets and Torrent skins also coming to PS5, Xbox and PC.
items.content:
Acclaimed action RPG debuts on Nintendo Switch 2; new content including two classes, new armor sets and torrent skins come to ELDEN RING on all platforms

ELDEN RING™ Tarnished Edition , the open world action RPG from FromSoftware Inc . and Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc ., is now available on Nintendo Switch™2 .

The game invites Nintendo players to enter the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow , bringing the original game that received more than 400 Game of the Year nominations bundled with the critically acclaimed expansion ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree to the console.

For the first time, players can experience FromSoftware ’s epic RPG on a Nintendo platform, experiencing its unforgettable gameplay moments and exploring its vast story and universe in docked or handheld mode.

ELDEN RING players across all platforms can also enjoy all-new content starting today, including new classes , gear , and Torrent skins featured in ELDEN RING™ Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2 and available for purchase for ELDEN RING on PlayStation 5 , XBOX Series X|S , and PC via Steam .

In ELDEN RING ™ Tarnished Edition, players will chart their own path in the vast and seamless world of the Lands Between , on foot or riding Torrent , their trusted Spectral Steed. Exploration is endless in this world full of wonders, but dangers lurk around every corner.

The Nintendo title also bundles in the acclaimed expansion Shadow of the Erdtre e, featuring an epic new adventure expanding on the story of the original, where players step into the Realm of Shadow, following in the footsteps of Miquella .

ELDEN RING™ Tarnished Edition also features brand new content, introducing two new Starting Classes , the Heavy Knight and the Idus Knight , along with four new armor sets that include two new starting class sets.

For the first time, players can also customize Torrent , choosing from three new appearance options.

The new content is also available for purchase on other platforms as the Tarnished Pack .

The original ELDEN RING sold more than 30 million units , introducing a vast, dark fantasy world as imagined by Hidetaka Miyazaki , creator of the DARK SOULS video game series, and George R.R. Martin , author of The New York Times’ best-selling fantasy series, “A Song of Ice and Fire.”

With ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition , Nintendo players will experience the unforgettable journey to become the Elden Lord , facing off against incredible challenges as they chart their path across sprawling environments, whether on foot or riding Torrent , their trusted Spectral Steed.

In the included expansion ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree , players embark on an entirely new adventure, facing a journey where they may need to leave their grace behind as they unravel the sinister dark side of the ELDEN RING story .

ELDEN RING is available on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, Xbox One, PS4 and PC

Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

    [/*]

  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.

    [/*]

  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

    [/*]

The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows: Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Weapons

    [/*]

    [/*]

  • Wooden Greatshield / Cuckoo Greatshield / Redmane Greatshield / Golden Greatshield / Crucible Hornshield / Dragonclaw Shield / Eclipse Crest Greatshield / Jellyfish Shield / One-Eyed Shield → Increased guard boost.

    [/*]

  • Haligtree Crest Greatshield → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased the time before an attack can be performed with a right-hand weapon immediately after attacking with this weapon equipped in the left hand.

    [/*]

Skills

  • Parry → Improved parry performance. → Reduced the time before various actions can be performed after activation when used with Daggers, Curved Swords, or Small Shields.

Sorceries

Incantations

PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments

Weapons

Incantations

Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where critical hits dealt with Great Katana weapon types had lower-than-expected power against large enemies. Fixed a bug where jumping attacks with Great Katana weapon types could be parried.

PC-Only Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug that prevented camera control with the mouse during NPC dialogue when using keyboard and mouse controls Fixed a bug in the "Keyboard/Mouse Settings" section of the system menu in which selecting the reset option did not restore various settings to their defaults The version number shown in the lower-right corner of the title screen after applying this update will be as follows:

We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy ELDEN RING more comfortably. Thank you for your continued support.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition review: Still a must-play title on the Switch 2
items.summary: Return to the Lands Between in FromSoftware’s fantasy epic on Nintendo Switch 2. Read the Empire review.
items.content:
by James Dyer | Updated on 27th August 2026 at 1.13pm Follow Empire on Google Platform: Nintendo Switch 2

When Hidetaka Miyazaki’s Demon’s Souls landed back in 2009, it forever altered the gaming landscape. A punishingly difficult, absurdly opaque game that made no effort to explain its mechanics, nor accommodate less capable players (dying just makes the game harder ), it set the stage for FromSoftware’s incredibly successful series of dark fantasy RPGs, each sharing similar mechanics, difficulty and mournful atmosphere. With that title, the ‘soulslike’ was born, but in 2022, with the release of Elden Ring , the formula was finally perfected.

A sweeping, open-world title that broadened the traditional soulslike canvas beyond anything before it, Elden Ring is a towering monument to inspired game design. The vast geography of The Lands Between lends players the feeling of being able to go literally anywhere at any time — if you can see a distant fortress or a mist-shrouded mountain peak on the far horizon then you’d better believe that, atop your trusty steed Torrent, you can find your way there and explore what lies within.

Four years after it debuted on Playstation, Xbox and PC, this magnificent game now makes its debut on Nintendo’s portable handheld in the form of this Tarnished Edition. Essentially a bundle of the base game and its similarly colossal expansion, Shadow Of The Erdtree , along with a few minor cosmetic additions, now playable in the palm of your hand. Except, if you’ve been paying attention, then you’ll know it seemed very much on course for absolute disaster. Early play sessions revealed a port so jerky as to be almost unplayable, clearly stretching the Switch 2’s hardware to breaking point. A lot has clearly happened since then, however, as we’re delighted to report that, in its final form, the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring is near faultless. Aside from some minor pop-in and very occasional slowdown when there’s a particularly large horde of dragons, trolls and assorted soldiery on screen, the frame rate remains buttery smooth throughout, with visual polish that, while not quite on a par with a high end PC or PS5, makes the game look absolutely gorgeous, whether in handheld mode or docked to a big screen TV.

The Tarnished additions boil down to three new customisable looks for your mount (including golden Tree Sentinel attire, complete with clanking plates as you gallop) picked up at various points in the story, four new armour sets (including the rakish Lucatiel set last seen in Dark Souls 2 ), and two new starting classes. Of the latter, the Idus Knight is a lightweight dexterity class with a long but nimble blade, while the chonky Heavy Knight lives up to its name, clad head to toe in plate and wielding a giant, two-handed scimitar. None of these additions have a huge bearing on the gameplay and while the two starting classes can make for a slightly more varied early game, by the time you step foot outside of Limgrave, you’ll likely have moved on towards whatever endgame build you were considering anyway. It’s also worth noting that all of the Tarnished Edition upgrades are available on existing consoles for a nominal DLC fee anyway, so there’s no need for completists to pick up the port just to have them. The only question here, is do you want to play Elden Ring on the Switch 2?

Few games have managed such a feeling of overwhelming scope and scale.

If you’ve never yet had the pleasure then the answer is a resounding ‘yes’. Four years on and Elden Ring has lost none of its majesty, more than having earned its place among the pantheon of the greatest games every made. Even those Ninty fans who’ve never yet sampled a soulslike and could be put off by the notorious difficulty should give this a try. The freedom to go anywhere means you’re rarely left bashing your head against the same insurmountable boss. Getting your arse handed to you? Go explore that distant forest, or delve into an underground city until you’re feeling stronger. The addition of spirit summons makes things yet more accessible than Souls past, too. Found through various hidden ashes, these let you summon (and upgrade) assistance for major boss fights without having to wait for other player to answer your call for help. Taking down a giant, sword-wielding lava lizard with a pack of spectral wolves (or a knight, a pair of puppets, or gaggle of greatshield-wielding skeletons) is no less rewarding than facing them solo and allows even players of modest ability to comfortably progress the game’s main story.

The story itself is as nebulous as that of all FromSoftware games, with dense background lore (here provided by George R R Martin), gleaned largely through item descriptions. But the central narrative isn’t the draw here so much as the environment itself and everything in it. There’s a dizzying assortment of enemies to put to the sword (or axe, or spell, or flaming incantation) as you progress through the world, but the primary joy here is in simple exploration. As you make your way through the castles of Limgrave, the watery expanse of Liurnia, the festering wastelands of Caelid, the gilded Royal Capital of Leyndell and far, far beyond, the vast landscape offers up a treasure trove of easily-missed nooks and crannies. Mines hidden in the crook of mountain passes, catacombs ensconced behind illusory walls, even entire play areas that you could easily miss in a single run-through if not taking your time to follow every path, scour every dead end or follow the silvery clues left by players who have come before. Few games have managed such a feeling of overwhelming scope and scale such that you could sink several hundred hours into exploring, while only turning up a fraction of what the game has to offer.

Put simply, Elden Ring is a must-play title and if this is your first opportunity to set foot in The Lands Between then we advise you to jump in with both feet. The Switch 2 port proves an unexpected triumph, too, capable of running this colossal game while losing precious little in the jump from big screen to handheld (though don’t expect your battery to last much more than a couple of hours playing this one). With the Shadow Of The Erdtree DLC providing more game hours than the majority of full-priced games, the Tarnished Edition represents incredible value, too. This is one Elden Ring to rule them all.

items.title: How to utterly embarrass yourself while "playing" Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Look: although I have the privilege of writing about video games for this fine outlet, this does not, by any measure, mean I am always good at said video games. Everyone here on the Nintendo Everything team has a genre or two they know like the back of their hand, and I can tell you with complete certainty that Soulslike...
items.content:
Look: although I have the privilege of writing about video games for this fine outlet, this does not, by any measure, mean I am always good at said video games. Everyone here on the Nintendo Everything team has a genre or two they know like the back of their hand, and I can tell you with complete certainty that Soulslike games are not my area of expertise. Regardless, the Nintendo Switch 2 port of Elden Ring and its Shadow of the Erdtree expansion – now bundled as the Tarnished Edition – remains one of the biggest third-party releases on the console this year, and I figured this would be a great opportunity to see if I was cut out for the challenge of one of 2022’s top-rated games.

Spoilers: I was not cut out for said challenge.

If you want to learn all about how to make an absolute fool of yourself while playing Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2, read on.

Elden Ring has a remarkably robust character creator that lets you adjust practically every pore of your warrior’s face. I can’t recall the last time I played a game in which I had so many distinct ways to negligibly adjust the size and positioning of a character’s nose and nostrils. And of course, all of this is a critical step towards getting immersed in the adventure to come.

I probably should have spent the same amount of time considering my character’s class. I opted to go into this game completely blind, so I just flipped through the list of classes and picked the one that seemed the most relevant to how I would normally play an action RPG, ultimately landing on the Bandit class. This seemed to be wise at the outset, because I figured that having a bow as well as a blade would be useful, probably leaving me well-equipped for most foes I would encounter in the early game.

While it wasn’t a horrible choice, I did find myself wishing pretty quickly that I had opted for a build with some more oomph. Having a knife that I could swing quickly felt good, as it allowed me to be nimble, but at least in the early game I didn’t get a ton of use out of having a bow on hand. Meanwhile, the character I made – a snow-haired stud I named Alabaster – spent 80% of his screen time with his face obscured by armor. Go figure. The good news is that, as the game progresses, there are plenty of ways to customize both your playstyle and your look, so you’re not locked into anything major.

How this version of Elden Ring might perform has been the subject of much conversation prior to launch. A world as sprawling and moody as The Lands Between is typically something I’d want to experience on the biggest screen possible. So it’s a real shame that I spent as much time fighting the game’s frame rate as I did fighting Godrick Knights – in docked mode, at least.

It’s not unplayable by any means, but it’s also far from perfect. Elden Ring’s docked frame rate heavily fluctuates depending on what is happening onscreen; generally it seemed like the more interesting the environment was, the more often I would encounter issues. There were times when it was so noticeable that it even made Alabaster’s running animation look a bit stilted. The game itself looks really good on the big screen – although not quite comparable to other platforms in terms of fine details – but given the scale of the world, the density of foliage and foes, and the very impressive lighting effects, it’s an understandable compromise.

In handheld mode, though, the game looks and runs immaculately. It’s a bewildering experience playing a game like this on such a slim device, and the fact that it looks as crisp and runs as smooth as it does in this mode is truly a miracle. I would also say that the smaller screen helps mask some of the DLSS and (what appears to be) dynamic resolution scaling better than while playing in docked mode.

I mean, sure, that giant tentacle monster slithering along the beach doesn’t look like a friendly fella, but it’s in the game’s opening section of the map. The developers wouldn’t seriously place such a high level foe right in the way of a player who is just trying to wander of the beaten path only a little, would they?

I know I shouldn’t be too surprised that Elden Ring doesn’t hesitate to destroy players who get a little too big for their britches, but it’s not just the big beasts that will KO you. Just about anything in this game can pose a serious threat if you are underleveled, underequipped, or underskilled as a player. I definitely felt like I fit into all three of those categories… well, the entire time I spent playing Elden Ring, really.

This game, in fact, does have quite a few similarities to Nintendo’s highly acclaimed Zelda adventure. Extremely sparse storytelling that’s mostly delivered as a by-product of exploration? Check. A cool horse? Check. Picking up resources to craft stuff and cook? Check. A wide open world that is so unfathomably massive that you wonder if you will ever possibly see everything in it? Check.

So, you’ll have to forgive my muscle memory as I repeatedly tried to climb things that could not be climbed (read: most things), jump over things that could not be jumped over, and casually wander into places that, apparently, are always filled with dangerous creatures that can wreck me in about 2 hits. In the opening area? And people play these games… for fun?!

Very early on in Elden Ring, I stumbled across a little camp of soldiers across from a huge castle gate. With my (theoretically) lighter and stealthier build, I figured I could probably just off them one by one without raising the alarm. I also figured there was probably some good stuff tucked away in there that would help me not be so much of a pushover.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition review – A great port of a phenomenal game
Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Switch 2 means you can now touch grace AND grass
Game Review: Elden Ring – Tarnished Edition (Switch 2)
Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Switch 2 Impression
items.summary: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition brings FromSoftware's acclaimed RPG to Switch 2. Despite some performance issues, the new content and portability make this version worth considering.
items.content:
by Imani Jones · Published August 26, 2026 · Updated August 24, 2026

For RPGamers with even a passing interest in this acclaimed game, Tarnished Edition provides a convenient new way to experience it.

I’ve been playing FromSoftware games since Demon’s Souls on the PS3, which means I’ve had a front-row seat to the studio’s evolution from a cult favorite developer into one of the most influential names in modern RPGs. The richly atmospheric and methodical design of Demon’s Souls laid the groundwork for Dark Souls , Bloodborne , Sekiro , and finally Elden Ring , a game that took everything FromSoftware had spent years refining and expanded it to a much larger scale. Elden Ring is, without question, one of the giants of this generation; its enormous world, memorable bosses, seemingly endless build possibilities, and extraordinary freedom in how players approach its challenges represent FromSoftware at its absolute best. I’ve spent a considerable amount of time with Elden Ring across its various iterations, so approaching Tarnished Edition is mostly about seeing how well the experience translates to Switch 2 and what its new content brings to the table.

The Tarnished Edition adds two new starting classes, the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight, alongside four new armor sets and three customization skins for Torrent, the player’s mount. The Idus Knight was the first class tested, followed by the Heavy Knight, and the difference between the two is apparent at the start. The Idus Knight is an agile, Dexterity-focused warrior from the land of Idus who starts at Level 7, making the class a natural fit for players already comfortable with Elden Ring ‘s dodge-focused combat and familiar with the game as a whole. The Heavy Knight starts at Level 10 and instead leans heavily into Strength, with bulky steel armor and a large scimitar providing a more forgiving start for players who are new to the game. These classes primarily affect the beginning of the game and do not lock players into any particular playstyle; as with other Souls games, stats, equipment, and builds can be adapted considerably as the journey progresses.

Interestingly, the Idus Knight starts with only 6 Arcane, the lowest of any starting class. This gives the class the lowest starting Discovery as well as the lowest resistance to Death Blight, while its low overall investment in Arcane leaves it particularly well suited to builds that want to minimize unnecessary stats. The practical impact of the lower Discovery is very small, so players looking to optimize their builds may actually appreciate how efficiently the Idus Knight distributes its starting attributes. Overall, the Heavy Knight is an excellent option for those who prefer a pure melee build, with its starting stats reflecting that approach, while the Idus Knight stands out as one of the best all-around starting classes in the game.

Beyond the new content, evaluating the Switch 2 version itself is just as important. Starting with docked mode, Bandai Namco has done an admirable job bringing Elden Ring to the Switch 2, although there are some significant performance issues to consider. The game targets 30 fps, though frame rates can drop noticeably while exploring the map, particularly as the system has to handle larger areas and more detailed environments. In some ways, the inconsistent performance is reminiscent of Bloodborne . Textures and overall visual detail are also noticeably reduced compared to other versions, although the lower resolution is not severe enough to prevent the game from looking generally fine. Thankfully, performance is much more stable during boss fights, where the action remains responsive. Despite these limitations, Tarnished Edition is perfectly playable in docked mode, and the scale of what has been brought to the Switch 2 remains impressive.

Handheld mode experiences many of the same performance issues, with frame rates dipping significantly during exploration. The reduced texture quality, on the other hand, is far less noticeable on the Switch 2’s smaller screen. More importantly, handheld mode represents the single biggest advantage of this version, as Elden Ring can finally be taken on the go without relying on streaming. The Joy-Con controllers are a little less suited to the precise demands of a Souls game than the Pro Controller, however, and the analog sticks can feel overly sensitive at first. This takes some adjustment, but once accustomed to the controls, Elden Ring remains perfectly playable in handheld mode.

Elden Ring has always been about freedom. Freedom to build a character however you want, freedom to approach its challenges in countless ways, and above all, freedom to explore the Lands Between at your own pace. Tarnished Edition takes that further, giving players the freedom to play the game wherever they go. Like many other open-world games on Switch 2, there are significant technical issues, but the fact that a game of this scale can run natively on a handheld at all is incredible. For those who have already experienced Elden Ring elsewhere, that may not be enough to justify another purchase, but for RPGamers with even a passing interest in this acclaimed game, Tarnished Edition provides a convenient new way to experience it. Elden Ring was designed around the idea of going wherever the road leads; now, that road can go almost anywhere.

Disclosure: This article is based on a copy of the game provided by the publisher.

items.summary: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is one of, if not the, best third-party ports for Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
By Jake Valentine Published Aug 26, 2026, 10:00 AM EDT Jake Valentine is a Contributor at DualShockers with more than two decades of experience covering the video game industry. Since 2004, he has written about games across news, reviews, guides, lists, interviews, and event coverage, with experience covering major shows, preview events, breaking news, and one-on-one developer interviews.

Before joining DualShockers, Jake contributed to Outrun Gaming , GameRant , and The Game Fanatics . He has also worked in editorial, brand management, and operations roles, giving him a broad perspective on both games coverage and digital media. He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Electronic Media and Broadcasting .

on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap As I was installing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on my Nintendo Switch 2, I had two primary concerns:

That first concern is, admittedly, silly. Of course, Elden Ring still holds up as an incredible gaming experience that everyone needs to play. The second concern, however, is quite valid.

Between aesthetics, depth and immersion, these spaces are a fundamental part of their works' greatness.

For as good as the Switch 2's third-party support has been, some games have felt poorly optimized. Oblivion Remastered, which I played immediately before Elden Ring Tarnished Edition, is filled with several notable issues , all of which deal with the game's performance. It's not the only Switch 2 port to suffer from this fate, either.

Thankfully, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition doesn't suffer from the same flaws. Yes, there are some (at times, obvious) limitations due to the Nintendo Switch 2 hardware, but ultimately, this is still the same Elden Ring experience we fell in love with four years ago. In fact, I'd argue that those restraints allow the Tarnished Edition to reach the heights it does.

Close window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1848179905"] = '" Close "'; Without a successful open world, Elden Ring doesn't succeed. Its ability to utilize boss difficulty as a way to encourage players to explore the rest of the map is a natural fit that stays true to the Soulslike genre . FromSoftware was courteous enough, too, to populate The Lands Between with plenty to see or do. Every time I play through the game, it feels like I'm finding something new.

Before I continue to lavish deserved praise on Elden Ring's open world, which has already been done plenty of times, let's not waste any more time. Elden Ring Tarnished Edition performs far better than I ever expected it to . Will it match Steam Deck performance? Absolutely not. It is, however, a well-put-together port that doesn't detract from the experience. Visually, the game doesn't compare to PC, PS5, or XBOX. Then again, I didn't need it to look as good. I just needed it to perform smoothly, and it absolutely does.

This is still the same Elden Ring experience we fell in love with four years ago.

With that concern out of the way, it was time to once again return to The Lands Between, and I have to be honest: I completely forgot I was playing on the Switch 2 most of the time. Of course, it helps that its Pro Controller feels like an absolute dream and not some of the clunky and awkward controllers of Nintendo's past. Beyond that, the frame rate was surprisingly stable, and the game looked just as good as I remember it.

If Tarnished Edition didn't come together here, then everything falls apart. What makes Elden Ring such an unforgettable experience is being able to explore the open world with little to no restrictions. Unless you're talking about enemies that constantly humble you, of course. I'm still able to play the game as I see fit, whether it's through optimized builds and preparation or just winging it. The game's tech doesn't hold you back or introduce restrictions. Failure is never due to the game's frame rate dropping or not responding either, so don't go out there trying to use that as an excuse for your deaths.

All that said, don't go out there expecting things to be absolutely perfect. The Switch 2 is not as powerful as its counterparts, and FromSoftware had to do some creative problem-solving to get Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree running on Nintendo's console. For the most part, you'll experience worse draw distances and the occasional long-distance pop-ins. There weren't, however, any egregious technical issues during my time with the game.

Its resolution is what impressed me the most about Elden Ring Tarnished Edition. That was, honestly, the biggest issue I had with Oblivion Remastered: it looked nowhere near as polished or refined as its counterparts on PC, XBOX, or PlayStation 5. It felt like I was playing a PS2 port of a GameCube or Xbox game from back in the day. With Tarnished Edition, it feels like I'm playing the real deal, and there's just some magical hand-waving going on in the background to make everything work.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Review – A New Way To Experience A Classic
items.summary: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is excellent on the Nintendo Switch 2, but a few issues remain.
items.content:
Elden Ring has entranced minds, frustrated gamers, and created a sense of wonder since 2022. If you’ve never played Elden Ring, whether that’s because you were never interested or because you only owned a Switch, today’s your lucky day! Fellow Tarnished, your Switch 2 is ready for its first site of grace. Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition gives us two new character bases and my personal favorite, a chance to start the journey all over again. Game Name: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Platform(s): Xbox Series X/S, PS5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2 Reviewed on: Nintendo Switch 2 Developer: FromSoftware Publisher: Bandai Namco Release Date: August 28th, 2026 I am so happy to see that Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree are coming to the Switch 2. A new audience will fall to the whims of gravity, fighting an endgame boss at level one, and making their way to becoming Elden Lord. If you were dancing with the idea of getting a Switch 2, I would say that now is the time to buy. With how many titles are getting either a bump up in FPS, a remaster, or making their Switch 2 debut, it’s the perfect time to invest in this console.

Never in my wildest dreams did I think that Elden Ring would find its way to the Switch. I’m so excited for everyone whose only console is a Switch 2 to experience this game. Now, while I do have a bias for Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree (platinumed it twice, the first time on Xbox, the second time on Steam), there are still some things left to be desired with this port. Firstly, the lighting is incredibly dark in certain parts. When it comes to games and the ambiance they create, I’m a huge proponent of leaving the world as it was designed unless it needs to be changed by the player for accessibility reasons.

I would highly recommend ramping up the lighting in settings, then adjusting image quality and changing it to your preferred setting from there. When I first started in Castleward Tunnel, it was incredibly dark; I couldn’t see much besides the site of grace, identifiers like the way to the boss, and the way I came into the tunnel. When I changed the settings, I felt the change was only incremental, and not substantially helpful. I could see a bit more, but it was still dark. Another thing that I thought would have been fixed this time around, is the ability to enhance the font-size in Elden Ring and its DLC. Launching on a new console has its trials and tribulations, but with how big FromSoftware is, I would have expected them to amp up the accessibility features this time around. If you can add two new classes, you can add accessibility that helps players maneuver throughout the beautiful world you’ve built. I’ve always been a critic of FromSoftware’s accessibility in Elden Ring. I guess I should just put these foolish ambitions to rest.

So why now, why get Elden Ring now? Having been available for four years on Xbox, PS5, and PC, why release this game on a new system now and not when it first launched? Now I don’t have interviews in my back pocket to pull out for this review to give you a definitive answer, but I do have an educated guess as to why. Firstly, reaching a wider audience is key. FromSoftware probably saw a gap in the market that wasn’t being filled by Elden Ring and wanted to fix that. Also, exclusives are a big move in the FromSoftware playbook; that’s not to say that’s a negative thing, it just is what it is.

In the Switch 2 version of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, there are two new classes available, Idus Knight and Heavy Knight. Much like the console exclusivity of Bloodborne or Demon’s Souls to the PlayStation, having classes locked behind a Switch 2 copy of Elden Ring will be reason enough for people to buy it. The two new classes, by the way, are incredibly fun to play around with. Just imagine a bleed build with the Idus Knight? Do I think the exclusivity of two classes is a bit much, yes, but I also think It might be there as an incentive to buy Elden Ring on the Switch 2. Amongst a plethora of things, come over to the dark side, we have NPC’s with main character syndrome, and an entrancing world to get lost in.

As for my experience and how the game flowed on the Switch 2, I didn’t find any major issues. Other than what I’ve mentioned, it was like I was playing Elden Ring on the PC or console post-patches. No, not the annoying, kick you down a hole Patches. Margit the Fell Omen was just as mad as ever that I was there, and Melina created a cozy spot near a site of grace for me to sit. I would catch myself getting lost in the world, looking back at the clock, and two hours had passed.

Playing this game was incredibly smooth with stable performance. I was crossing my fingers that everything would work the way it’s supposed to, and I’m so happy that it did. Moving through the world, I was trying to do several things at once to “break the game” so to speak. Like riding Torrent while fighting enemies that you find out in the world, or randomly falling from great heights, just to see if the game would crash, and there was nothing. No crashes, blips, or even pop-ins. I think people who only own a Switch 2 or who own multiple consoles, plus a Switch 2, will love the port of this game. While, of course, there are no achievements, it’s nice to roam the world, explore, experiment with builds, and do things you might not want to do on your main build.

As someone who owns every console (plus a Steam Deck and PC), the only thing that gets tricky is remembering which buttons are which when going from playing PS5 to the Switch 2. Besides getting used to the button layout, this port is everything I could have hoped for. I really love the fact that the pop-ins are non-existent, which is rare for a lot of Switch games to not have on release, or before the first wave of patches come out.

I took a look at how the game performs across console, PC, Steam Deck, and now the Switch 2. I’d like to focus in for a moment comparing the game’s performance on the Switch 2 versus the PC. Since the PC is what I have the most hours in, sitting at 120 hours, I feel like it’s the fairest piece of tech to use as a comparison. When the PC version of Elden Ring launched, it was a mess; now, keep in mind, I didn’t get the PC version until a year later. While several patches came out, and efforts were taken to make the best possible version it could be, it was still a hot mess.

Playing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 feels like FromSoftware learned from the PC release and shipped a smooth, day-one version with no performance issues. Other than the issues I mention in this review, which I feel are more quality-of-life fixes than a day-one patch. The Switch 2 version, by far, runs smoother than the PC version when it launched. While the PC version of Elden Ring runs really well, there will still be minor performance issues from time to time. With the Switch 2 version, I feel that this might be the best the game has been optimized. Who knows, I might find some issues later on, but as of now, the performance of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is incredible!

I greatly enjoyed my time so far with the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring! While the image quality/brightness suffers a bit in handheld mode, I saw no visible bugs, issues, pop-ins, or anything that hindered the gameplay experience. If you’ve been wanting to check out Elden Ring and its DLC, but had no way to play until now, I would highly recommend investing in Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition!

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition will release August 28th, 2026, for Nintendo Switch 2

Review Disclosure Statement : Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition was provided to us by Bandai Namco. For more information on how we review video games and other media/technology, please review our Review Guideline/Scoring Policy .

With two new classes exclusive to the Switch 2, FromSoftware brings the best day-one performance of Elden Ring I’ve ever seen. While the image quality, brightness, and ability to change the font size were lacking, this port runs incredibly well!

items.summary: After timid previews, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition
items.content:
After timid previews, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition's final form runs perfectly fine on Switch 2 and impresses with the visuals

(Image credit: FromSoftware, Bandai Namco Entertainment) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elden Ring remains one of the most important and best RPGs of the decade and it's easy to talk me into replaying it. This made a new journey to the Lands Between on Nintendo Switch 2 enticing before I'd even touched the port. While early reports last year weren't exactly encouraging, I trusted FromSoftware to take its time and eventually deliver a conversion worthy of an Elden Lord.

After a more convincing showing in early 2026 , we hoped for the best. Ahead of The Duskbloods ' launch on Switch 2, the Hidetaka Miyazaki-led studio needed a major win that makes it clear Nintendo's latest console isn't getting second-grade material. Thankfully, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition makes an excellent first impression and feels perfectly fine to play... As long as you're happy with a conservative framerate lock and no major additions.

What it's like beating Elden Ring twice a week for 4 years: "I think it's the greatest game that's ever been made"

Despite its cross-generation nature and more than a few aging elements, Elden Ring wasn't a guaranteed win on Nintendo's second hybrid console. Whether it was the in-house engine's limitations or a lack of optimization, this (otherwise) excellent action RPG wasn't a great performer on PS5 and Xbox Series X. A constant 60 FPS lock isn't possible even on Performance mode, so everyone who played Elden Ring on consoles has gotten used to its unevenness.

This could've spelled doom for the Switch 2's Tarnished Edition. Yet the final result is visually convincing. Smart sacrifices prevent it from presenting a lesser version of the gorgeous world FromSoftware introduced in 2022. None of its visual identity is lost, and even with an obviously lower graphical preset when running it in handheld versus docked mode (compared in the gallery below), the final image output is shockingly sharp.

Elden Ring Tarnished Edition in handheld mode (Image credit: Bandai Namco Entertainment, FromSoftware) Elden Ring Tarnished Edition in docked mode (Image credit: FromSoftware, Bandai Namco Entertainment) Image 1 of 2 View Original

Though Elden Ring Tarnished Edition on Switch 2 lacks visual modes (or framerate targets), playing it handheld automatically cuts distant shadows, fog density, asset level of detail, lighting, and, of course, resolution. The overall visual features survive the transition, but lighting is an obvious change; the Lands Between seem a bit dimmer if you're not playing docked, at least when exploring outside.

Oblivion Remastered on Switch 2 is a miracle port – and a reminder the RPG still isn't fixed New Elden Ring DLC and Nintendo Switch 2 Tarnished Edition finally get a release date The 20 best Switch 2 games to play in 2026 The presence of so many visual changes versus a simpler resolution downgrade to hit a 30 FPS target – yes, as far as I can tell, it doesn't go higher than that – may be explained by the fact FromSoftware's engine isn't compatible with DLSS. Frustratingly, the press materials provided by Bandai Namco neither confirm nor deny what's happening under the hood, so I have to assume the lower graphical preset makes up for the lack of that upscaling crutch.

In any case, the resolution looks to be 1080p on both TV and the console's own screen. It's among the sharpest-looking third-party ports I've played so far on Switch 2 even in its more compromised form, that's for sure. In fact, I'd say it looks better than it did on Xbox Series S, which makes me think some sort of upscaling might be involved. As an extra, the HDR support, even on the Switch 2's below-average screen, gives a depth to darker areas and shaded environments that's often quite remarkable.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

It's among the sharpest-looking third-party ports I've played so far on Switch 2

With a 30 FPS lock in place that generally holds steady, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition on Switch 2 actually feels a lot like playing Bloodborne on the PS4.

Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring , a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' Mistfall Hunter's demo might finally convince me, a souls sicko, to give extraction games a proper go—even if it's more modern God of War than Nightreign The next game in a huge Chinese action RPG series has plenty of action, but I hope it hasn't totally abandoned the RPG What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
